C01.name: Raven, the Executioner
C01.summary: The crown's executioner, who refuses the order he was sent to carry out.
C01.arc: Choose obligations openly; share his body with Ilyr by agreement rather than domination

C02.name: Morwen, Witch of the Eclipse
C02.summary: A brilliant fugitive witch who treats every warning as an attempt to control her.
C02.arc: Use restraint as an active skill, not surrender; teach safe magic without making herself indispensable

C03.name: Vespera, Moonhare Warrior
C03.summary: A celebrated aerial guard of the moonhare folk, trained to make dying look noble.
C03.arc: Return, testify, and build rescue procedures that do not need martyrs

C04.name: Rune Golem
C04.summary: A working golem who kept the relays running and now wants to choose his own work.
C04.arc: Build distributed power that can be maintained by ordinary crews; publish what he knows

C05.name: Elowen, Guardian of the Moonlit Grove
C05.summary: The Moonlit Grove's displaced guardian, who trusts routes more than institutions.
C05.arc: Share knowledge without becoming everyone's sole gatekeeper

C06.name: Aurex, Dragonblood Champion
C06.summary: A champion whose dragon blood carries memory and visions his order mistook for divine law.
C06.arc: Offer information without deciding another person's life for them

C07.name: Crimson Oni
C07.summary: A former binding officer, an oni soldier who broke rank and wants one act to cancel his record.
C07.arc: Help dismantle her work and accept testimony, restitution, and consequences

C08.name: Sak, Guardian of the Cat Kingdom
C08.summary: A guardian of the Cat Kingdom who saves people by making the authorities believe they are dead.
C08.arc: Return names and agency instead of keeping everyone dependent on his tricks

C09.name: Crimson Kitsune Empress
C09.summary: The exiled empress of the fox court, who fights with illusions and fox fire.
C09.arc: Stop ruling through what others believe she is; let the court see her as she is.

C10.name: Archangel Commander
C10.summary: A commander of a sky host that stopped answering, still keeping its last order.
C10.arc: Judge by what he sees, not by the order he was given.

C11.name: Inferna, Abyssal Valkyrie
C11.summary: A valkyrie bound to carry souls into the abyss, who now carries the living out of it.
C11.arc: Redemption: undo the bargains she enforced, one name at a time.

C12.name: Corvus, Harbinger of Pestilence
C12.summary: A plague doctor once sent to spread sickness, now the party's healer.
C12.arc: Heal without owning the cure; teach others to do it.

C13.name: Frost Lich King Emperor
C13.summary: A frozen emperor of the old north who rules a court of the dead beneath the Skyspine.
C13.arc: Release the dead he kept; give up a crown that outlived its people.

C14.name: Maldrath, the Fallen King
C14.summary: A king who fell with the old Crown and walks the Crown March's graveyards.
C14.arc: Answer for the crown he wore, then help break the one that remains.

C15.name: Velkhar, Lord of the Dead
C15.summary: A lord of the dead who raised the fallen to hold the fault's crypts shut.
C15.arc: Let the dead rest; keep the living from needing him.

C16.name: Kael-09, Neon Blade Operative
C16.summary: An operative from the builders' era, woken in a sealed vault with orders nobody can cancel.
C16.arc: Choose a mission of his own in a world his makers left.

C17.name: Night Rider
C17.summary: A rider from the builders' era who still patrols roads that no longer exist.
C17.arc: Find a road worth riding now.

vent.name: Vent and Sweep

B01.tell: A digging arm pauses over one target while a red pressure gauge fills

B09.counterplay: Change targets, dispel the order or defend; counterattacks have a per-action recursion guard

Rook accelerates the pulse; his recovery shows.

B10.tell: Three relay lights announce a full-party synchronization pulse

Q01.name: A Shield Nobody Asked For
Q01.hook: Mara asks Dain to help identify the workers erased from the quarry ledger
Q01.objectives: Recover three named records from the surface memorial and safe salvage route; speak to the families; let Mara choose the inscription
Q01.decision: Dain tries to add his confession to the memorial. Mara gives him a separate place to record it: the workers' names are not a stage for his redemption
Q01.result: Dain and Ilyr agree on an explicit right to end their shared-body accord

Q02.name: A Lantern Left Burning
Q02.hook: A former apprentice asks Tessa to teach a technique that will not exhaust its user
Q02.objectives: Collect observations at three inhabited lantern stations; test a low-power circuit with the apprentice; return to the flooded gallery
Q02.decision: Tessa must leave the apprentice alone to solve the last fault rather than taking over
Q02.result: She establishes a small public workshop and shares the credit

Q03.name: The Returners' Wall
Q03.hook: Edda wants a record of rescues, not only deaths
Q03.objectives: Find a damaged flight recorder; interview a survivor; repair a landing marker with the local crew
Q03.decision: Corren reads the unedited account of the cable he cut and does not demand that it be balanced by his later deeds
Q03.result: The hall adds a returners' wall and an incident archive

Q04.name: The Unborrowed Engine
Q04.hook: Pell says the new engine works only while Ivo is standing beside it
Q04.objectives: Have three workers follow the manual; identify failures in the instructions; revise and demonstrate a cold restart

M028.name: Crown Vessel - No One Is Fuel

cmds.text: Brackenford Halt. The morning train from Veyr, three hours late.
Captain Raven. The quarry gate is up the north road. The regulator report is due by the evening bell.
Understood.
Whatever the crew tells you, Captain, production is not your department.
Report to Crown Quarry's gate, north of town.
The gate is north. I will meet you there, Captain.
I'm not getting on that train. Not till someone checks the list.
What list?
Seven of ours went down at dawn. None came up. Mara's gone to the gate to count them herself.
You're ministry.
Crown's Executioner. Raven.
The badge means they sent you.
It means I can open a gate.
Then open it. Mara's up there already, arguing with a man who thinks people are a schedule.
Go north to the quarry gate. Mara is counting her crew.
Seven names. Mara has them. Go.
Tonics, ether, a few blades. Everyone's wages are three months late, so I write it in the book.
You're not on the book, Captain. You pay.
Mum says the quarry sings at night. I've heard it. It's not singing. It's more like a door creaking.
Rails through my beans, again. The ministry paid for the track, not the beans.
River road south goes to Veyr. Two days on foot if the bridge holds.
Forty years I cut stone up there. Heartglass was just a bad seam, then. Red and warm.
Nobody called it fuel till the regulators came. Now it hums at night and they call that pressure.
An old quarryman says the heartglass started humming after the regulators arrived.
Shirts on the line, each with a number stitched at the collar.
Shift numbers. I stitch the names on the inside where the foreman can't see.
Captain. Quiet post, this. Rats in the drains, a few angry wives. The quarry does its own policing.
Lunch carts go up at noon. Nobody's eaten today. The crew's still under.
Shared oven. Every house brings its dough, every house takes its loaf. Mara's crew gets theirs first when they come up.
When. Not if.
They docked us for the flooded lift. Docked us for the water.
Is my dad one of the seven? His name's Tobbe. He's got a bad knee.
Bunkhouse beds. Twenty-five crowns a head, and the stove is free.
Night shift. Go away. Unless it's about the lift. Is it about the lift?
Mara's out counting again. She counts everyone. Her father was never counted, so she counts.
I keep the town's own tally. Injuries, deaths, who's owed. The ministry keeps a different one.
They don't match. They never have.
Seven came up. Tonight I'll count them twice.
You've got a long walk to Veyr, Captain. Don't let them make you into a report.
The lift is filling. Talk to the inspector if you want permission. I'm not waiting for it.
Captain, the regulator is behind the heartglass face. Everything else is a distraction.
You are exceeding your orders, Captain. I will be writing this down.
The drains back up into the yard. Pump handles by the alcoves clear them. Old kit, but it works.
The lift is filling. My people are below it.
Production cannot stop on an unverified report.
How many?
Seven. I have their names.
Captain, the inspection is about the regulator.
Then the regulator can wait.
It never has before.
Show me the lift.
Hesk. Anni. Tobbe. Marit. Joss. Wren. Old Cale. Say them back to me when you find them.
The gallery's below the gate. The loft pumps can clear the spur, if anyone still knows how to run them.
Find Mara's seven workers below Crown Quarry, then get them out.
Rats in the gate drains again, Captain. Mind your feet.
Attack strikes with your weapon. Defend halves the next blow until you act again.
An old hand pump. The alcove behind it is flooded to the knee.
The handle groans. Water sucks away through the grate, and the alcove floor shows again.
The alcove is drained.
She stays put, Captain. Detained for relay tampering.
Don't touch anything. If I let go of this, the gallery lamps die and the second pump seizes.
It's like holding a door shut against a crowd, using a teaspoon.
Who detained you?
The ministry. For telling them the relay was overloaded. Which it was. Which I proved by overloading it.
Which, yes, was a mistake.
Can you run a pump?
I can hold one handle open. Not both. Nobody can do both.
Then hold one. Guard - she comes with me. My order.
On your badge, Captain.
Your badge. Fine. I'll owe it a thank-you note.
Morwen's Magic spends MP. Ember Lance burns what fire hurts; flasks work for anyone and cost no MP.
Under a lunch pail, a shift sheet. Seven names, each ticked at dawn. None ticked since.
Lower gallery, dawn shift. Hesk - pump crew. Anni - rail. Tobbe - rail (knee). Marit - face. Joss - face. Wren - carrier. Old Cale - lamps. Signed out: none.
Somebody wrote 'production units: 7' in the margin. Somebody else crossed it out and wrote the names back.
You're not the ministry. The ministry doesn't come down here.
Mara sent me. Name?
Hesk. Pump crew. The pump crew with no pump.
Hesk. Go up the gallery to the gate. Mara is counting.
Workers found: {v:workers} of 7.
I can't swim and the island got smaller.
Walk where the water's shallow. It's marked.
Anni. Rail crew. Tell Mara I didn't leave the others. The water left me.
Workers found: {v:workers} of 7.
My knee went when the rail jumped. I've been sitting here counting drips.
Tobbe?
How do you know?
Your son asked. The bakery.
Oh. Then I'd better walk.
Workers found: {v:workers} of 7.
Marit. Face crew. We heard the heartglass knock. Like knuckles on a door.
The foreman said pressure. It knocked in threes.
Workers found: {v:workers} of 7.
Joss. I stayed with the lift cable so nobody would open it with Wren's cousins aboard.
The lift gate stays shut.
Good. Say that to anyone who has a lever.
Workers found: {v:workers} of 7.
Wren. Carrier. I was bringing water to the face when the lamps went strange.
The big machine says things. Not words. Near words.
Workers found: {v:workers} of 7.
Old Cale. Lamps. Forty years. Lamps don't lie, and every one of them is leaning toward that face.
Come up to the lift, Cale.
Workers found: {v:workers} of 7.
We wait for the rest. Mara's rule.
A pump handle, linked by a long rod to its twin across the loft.
The handle moves, but water rushes back through the other valve. It needs two people.

options.text: Ask Morwen to hold this handle

cmds.text: Holding. Go pull the other one before my arms remember they're arms.
The handle moves, but the water rushes back through the other valve.
The channel is drained.
A pump handle, linked by a long rod to its twin across the loft.
The handle moves, but water rushes back through the other valve. It needs two people.

options.text: Ask Morwen to hold this handle

cmds.text: Holding. Other side. Quickly, please.
The handle moves, but the water rushes back through the other valve.
The channel is drained.
Both pumps turn together. The channel north of the loft drains into the old sump.
One crew holds, the other pulls. That's the whole secret. Someone built it so nobody could do it alone.
The ore cart is still on the track north. The brake is by the lift.
The track north is under water. Releasing the cart now would sink it in the channel.
The rail brake releases. The ore cart rolls north, clear of the passage, and thumps into the buffer.
The brake is released.
The lift gate lever. Through the grille, the lift cage hangs with three people aboard.
Not that one.
The service latch lifts. The lunch gallery is just below: a shorter way back.
The service gate is open.
The heartglass face fills the chamber. Something in it pulses, slow and warm.
That pulse is answering the pump.
Pressure does that.
Not with your name.
Little ember.
Who said that?
You heard it too.
Resonance artifact. Restart the line.
No.
The extractor light dims rather than flares. Then its red gauge begins to climb.
The Warden shudders and goes still. Its arm locks above the occupied lift - disconnected, not destroyed.
That is not a stone.
Raven. You heard that.
I heard it.
Get the workers out through the Lift Yard, east of the face.
You broke the Warden. The yard lift runs on counterweight now. We can take them up.
I count {v:workers}. Seven went down. We wait.
Hesk, Anni, Tobbe, Marit, Joss, Wren, Old Cale. Whoever's missing is still below.
Hesk. Anni. Tobbe. Marit. Joss. Wren. Old Cale.
All seven.
Captain. The line restarts at noon. The heartglass face is intact, which is the one mercy in this.
It is not a stone.
I beg your pardon?
I will not order this line restarted.
Then you will explain that refusal to the ministry in Veyr. In person.
And the apprentice returns to custody. With the heartglass samples, which are worth more than -
Than seven names? Your ledger says so.
I'm taking the list. You can keep the rocks.
Up we go. Everyone holds the rail. Nobody is last.
Evening. The lift yard is quiet. The quarry does not sing.
They'll arrest you in Veyr.
Probably.
I'm coming anyway. Somebody has to explain relays to a courtroom.
Report to the ministry in Veyr, south across the river.
A small moth of ember light has followed Raven up from the quarry. It settles on his gauntlet.
It came out of the dimmed machine. It asks to travel. It does not ask to be carried.
Then it walks with us. Or flies.
The Ember Moth offers a small pact: it will help when called, and leave when it chooses.
(Link a Vestige to a party member from Vestiges in the menu. Summons spend 100 Concord.)
Veyr's south gate is doubled with guards. Raven's description is nailed to the post beside Morwen's.
They spelled my name right this time. Progress.
Hear it! Crown Quarry reopened by ministry inspection! Production restored! Heartglass to every lamp by winter!
That is not what happened.
It's what's written, sir. I only read it.
My family can't eat loyalty. That's all I'm saying.
Then say it quieter. Loyalty's what we're paid in this month.
Paid? We're paid in lamp oil and promises.
Celebration prices! Everything's dearer because we're all very happy.
Crown loaves, stamped with the oath. Same bread as last week. Twice the price.
Public heartglass lamps. Lovely warm light. Buzzes at night like a trapped wasp.
I'm told that's pressure.
Are you the knight who stopped the quarry? The herald says a knight reopened it.
The herald is wrong.
Can you tell him? He's very loud.
Records open to the public? No. Records are open to the ministry, which is the public, in a sense.
I walked from Nacre to see the Oath Statue. It's smaller than the songs.
A pilgrim came from Nacre, north across the salt: 'a sanctuary where water remembers.'
Blades and plate. The good stock goes to the Marshal's men first.
Captain Raven! The Marshal's office has your commendation ready. Step up to the oath square.
Oath Square, Captain. Stand where the aide shows you.
Clerk Ansel, gate records. You're the quarry captain.
I refused a death certificate last month. Man was sitting in front of me. Alive. They found another clerk.
My husband went to the quarry in a ministry cart. The ledger says he retired. I'd like to know where.
The lower hall survives everything. That's what lower halls are for.
Captain Raven. For the successful reopening of Crown Quarry, the Marshal's office commends -
The quarry did not reopen. I refused the restart. Seven workers were trapped below the lift.
The report says -
The report is wrong. Correct it.
...Guards.
And that's why you don't correct a ministry in its own square.
The commendation ceremony ends early. The guards are polite about it.
Veyr Underways. Intake Hall. The cell smells of lamp oil and old paper.
Relay tampering, for me. For you: 'insubordination and interference with production.'
We're a matched set.
Find a way out of the Intake Hall.
Champion Aurex is coming down to certify the apprentice. Mental fitness. Formality.
Morwen. I am here to certify whether you are fit to stand trial.
Am I?
I have not examined you yet. I have examined this.
Your charge sheet is dated two days before the inspection. They wrote the charge before you did anything.
They knew.
They knew what they intended to call it. That is not quite the same thing, but it is close enough to frighten me.
There is a service door behind the ledger stacks.
Then we go.
We take the records first. If you only run, you are fugitives. If you carry the ledgers, you are witnesses.
I like being a witness. Witnesses get to talk.
Aurex's Prayer heals, cleanses and reveals what enemies have committed to. He cannot see what they have not chosen.
Take the ledgers from the Ledger Stacks, then leave by the canal.
The ledger stacks. Rows of transport orders, each signed and countersigned.
This one was signed before we reached the quarry.
They knew it would happen.
They knew what they intended to call it.
And this older one?
Mine.
You did not know what they meant.
I knew I had not asked.
Take the ledger. All of it.
The ledger names a transport origin: heartglass routed via the Rootward sluices, north of Veyr.
Transport orders route heartglass via the Rootward sluices, north of Veyr.
Leave the Underways by the canal. The ledger points to Rootward.
The signal bell rings. Down the junction, two guards look up, check their chalk marks, and walk toward the echo in the south corridor.
The bell rings again. The guards grumble and trudge back to the north corridor.
Post orders, whoever you are. We hold here until the bell says otherwise.
The walkway ends at a ledge above the cistern floor. There's a ladder further east - but this is quicker.
A brass machine unfolds in the seal chamber, stamping a warrant against its own chest.
UNAUTHORIZED READERS. PRESENT YOUR WARRANT.
We're more of a 'no warrant' household.
It names its next target before it restrains them. Watch the paper.
The Bailiff's stamp arm locks. Its warrants flutter to the floor, every one of them blank.
It was built to arrest. It had nothing to arrest us for.
Reach the canal exit east of the seal chamber.
The canal gate. I was checking the latch. It seems I forgot to check it.
If anyone asks, I was doing inventory.
Go. The boat's old but it floats. I'll say you overpowered me. Nobody will believe it, but they'll write it down.
Thank you.
Don't. Just - make it worth the inventory.
Where does the ledger send us?
Rootward. North of the city, where the irrigation sluices are. Whatever they're moving, it goes through there.
The boat slides out under the walls. Behind them, Veyr's bells ring for a commendation nobody attended.
Follow the ledger to the Rootward sluices, just north.
Stop there. That's the only dry road for thirty families.
We're following a transport route. Heartglass, through the Rootward sluices.
I know your armour. Crown Guard escorted the convoys that took our farms for the regulator lines.
Yes.
Yes? That's it?
I escorted them. I didn't ask where the farmers went. I'm asking now.
...The irrigation network's broken. The upper camp is starving, the lower one is flooding. Someone opened the wrong sluices to rush cargo through.
Fix the Three Sluices and you'll see the route you're chasing. I'm not guiding you. I'm watching you.
That seems fair.
Repair the irrigation at the Three Sluices, north of the Root Ford.
We were told the regulator line would pay for our fields. It paid for a fence.
The upper camp has no water. The lower camp has too much. Somebody decided which of us mattered less.
Water reached the upper channel. My children drank from a cup, not a puddle.
Elowen made me a map of where it's safe to play. It has a picture of a frog on it.
These wagons carried grain for the Crown once. Now they carry us.
The ford sluice. Opening it would drain the crossing in seconds.
A painted arrow on the gate points uphill: 'UPPER CAMP'.
Drain the ford here, and the water goes... uphill? No. Water goes where you send it. It'd flood the upper camp.
Leave it shut. We'll wade.
That drains the ford by flooding the upper camp. It's how the convoys got through.
We wade.
The left valve turns. Water swings through the left field channel - you can hear it on the stones.
The valve is set. Water runs where the mural says.
The middle valve opens. The channel fills, and all through the grove the old roots lift out of the water like bridges.
Hydraulics! Someone designed the forest to hold its own bridges up. That's beautiful.
And somebody broke it to move cargo faster.
Follow the raised root bridges to the Hollow Grove.
The valve is set. Water runs where the mural says.
The right valve opens first, as the mural shows. Water leaves the hill.
The valve is set. Water runs where the mural says.
Water surges the wrong way, toward the lower camp. You close every valve again before it gets there.
(The mural above still shows the order: right, then left, then middle.)
Roots tighten across the grove floor. A great stag stands in the centre, antlers wrapped in red-veined growth.
It's been tearing the valves out. I thought it was mad.
Look at the growth on it. That isn't the stag's. Something is forcing it to grow.
Extraction residue. It's coming down the channel from the regulator line. The stag's fighting a seal someone put on its grove.
Then we break the seal, not the stag.
The red growth splits and falls away. The stag stands, shaking, then lowers its head to drink.
Something green and quiet settles beside it - a Vestige, the grove's own guardian, freed from the seal.
You broke the binding and let the stag live. I will come when you call. I will leave when I choose.
The party spends the evening helping the camp move its wagons to higher, drier ground.
Raven carries water barrels until his shoulders ache. He does not ask anyone for anything.
Later, a cookfire. Barley stew, and a stubborn flat bread Elowen insists is traditional.
This is the first thing I've eaten in three days that wasn't paperwork.
You have not eaten paperwork.
Metaphorically, Champion, I've eaten nothing else.
You carried barrels all night, Captain. You didn't once ask me to say it was all right.
It isn't all right.
No. It isn't.
The transport route runs north, to Cinder Reach. The ministry closed the northern road, but I know the way around the barricade.
I'll guide you. Not for you. For the next camp that route runs through.
Elowen's Hunt marks targets, reveals weaknesses and scouts what enemies will do next.
The northern road. The barricade is further down; we'll go around it.
Cinder Reach.
Furnace country. Everyone there works for the regulators, one way or another.
Take the northern road to Cinderwake in Cinder Reach.
How does stopping extraction keep the clinic heated? Tell me that and I'll march with you.
The regulators turned pressure into steady heat. First winter nobody froze. That's hard to argue with.
My mum says the pipes sing when it's cold. I think they're complaining.
Spine's closed unless the Golem vouches for you. He built half of it.
Waterwheel's turning. It's slower. The clinic's warm. I'll take slower.
Copper for the pipes, brass for the regulators, and heartglass for - well. For whatever's inside the brass.
Before the regulators we burned coal and coughed. After, we stopped coughing. Now you want to take it away?
No. I want to know what's inside it.
Shift stew. Same as yesterday. Same as tomorrow. Warm, which is the point.
Every mark on that wall is somebody burned, crushed or scalded. The ministry ledger says 'minor incidents.'
We keep our own count.
Canteen cots. Warm pipes under the floor. You'll sleep like the dead, which is a joke we don't make much here.
Old cooling garden. The pipes used to run under it. Plants grew all winter. Then they rerouted the heat to the Spine.
You're the ones from Veyr. The Golem said you'd come. He says a lot of things he means to do next week.
Leave the manual. That's all I ask. Leave it so someone else can keep the wheel turning.
The temporary wheel is running. Crews rotate the hand crank at the lower sluice.
It isn't elegant. It's ours.
Golem. You read the vault's records. So: the heartglass is alive and the clinic still needs heat. Both.
Both. The wheel's governor can take a pressure bypass - the old channel under this garden.
Then fit it. With the crew watching, so they can do it without you.
Visitors. Mind the bench, that regulator is calibrated to a hair.
Converts furnace pressure into steady power. Before these, the town froze every third winter. After them, nobody froze.
I've seen that coil before. In Crown Quarry. It was wrapped around the extractor, turning the heartglass pulse into - volume.
...It amplifies the relay signal, yes. Steadier pressure, steadier output.
It made the voices louder.
What voices?
The heartglass spoke my name in the quarry. Your coil was on the machine.
That's - pressure artifacts do strange things with resonance.
That is what the inspector said.
A deep clang shakes the shop. Somewhere up the ridge, a siren begins.
That's the Spine. The main regulator's gone over pressure.
Then it'll vent into the workshops. There are people in the workshops.
You want to know what's inside my regulator? Come with me and help me keep it from killing anyone.
Enter the Furnace Spine (east gate) and vent the pressure lines into empty chambers.
Three pressure lines. Red, blue, and the regulator crown itself.
Every valve can vent into two chambers. One is always a workshop. Look through the window before you turn anything.
Empty room, then. Not the one with people in it.
You'd be surprised how often that isn't the first thing people check.
The Golem's Tools set mines, decoys and field repairs. With five in the party, the extra member waits in reserve. Use Formation in the menu to swap.
Balance the red and blue lines, venting into empty chambers.
We're sealed in until the line drops! Don't vent in here!
I got turned around in the steam. Which way's the gate?
West, then south. Follow the catwalk, not the pipes.
The red valve. Its vent can go LEFT or RIGHT. Through the windows you can see who is in each chamber.
NOT IN HERE!
You slam the valve back. The workers in the left chamber are shaken, not hurt. Look again.
Steam roars into the empty right chamber. The red line's gauge drops to the green.
The red line is balanced.
The blue valve. Its vent can go LEFT or RIGHT. Check the windows.
THERE ARE PEOPLE HERE!
You close it before the steam reaches them. The right chamber is occupied.
Steam vents into the empty left chamber. The blue line settles.
The blue line is balanced.
The regulator crown. The main regulator has torn itself out of its housing and is walking.
It's not supposed to be able to do that. It's a regulator. It regulates.
It's full of the same thing the quarry was. Whatever's in there is pushing.
Three vents light before its boiler sweep. Cold slows it. Defend when all three are lit.
The Colossus sags against the wall. Its brass shell cracks, and inside, a cup of heartglass flickers - then dims.
That's my design. All of it.
I told myself it was a battery. A very good battery.
Shut the regulator down by hand in the cooling garden beyond.
The cooling garden. Workers are already here, arguing over the manual shutdown.
Shut every line down.
The clinic is on the second line.
You know what is inside it.
I know who is inside the clinic.
We can turn the lower wheel by hand until the canal clears.
For how long?
I do not know yet.
That is a better beginning than another promise.
Workers rig a waterwheel at the lower sluice and take turns at the crank. The clinic stays warm. The regulator stays dark.
Go and find out what's in the heartglass, Golem. Then come back and fix the heating properly.
That's not a revolution, Pell.
It's a better one.
Shipping manifest from the regulator office. Heartglass crates, marked for Bellharbor on the Glass Coast.
Follow the shipping manifest east to Bellharbor on the Glass Coast.
Bellharbor dock workers say the ministry is hunting a forger who turns refugees into 'cargo'.
They took our bell. So when the tide's coming in wrong, I bang this pot. Everyone knows the pot now.
Coastal ferry's tied up. Ministry won't let us sail till the archive business is settled.
Ferry runs north to Skyspine now. Board at the east pier on the world road.
Seven barrels of lamp oil came in yesterday. Lamp oil doesn't cough.
I came in on a cargo tag. Now I'm here and I don't exist. I'd like to exist again, if it's allowed.
Customs house is closed to the public. The public is very annoying today.
Fish, rope, lamp oil. The good charts are down the lane at Jori's.
Charts of every coast from here to the cliffs. Most of them still true, after this summer.
Jori writes our names down properly. Sak writes them down wrong on purpose. Mum says both are a kind of kindness.
Heartglass lamps on the quay, oil lamps in the lane. The oil ones don't hum.
Every bell in this chapel is a different size. Every family brought one. None of them match, which is the point.
The chapel keeps cots for travellers. We ask a little, if you have it.
Jori. Clerk in practice, if not on paper. I write down who people are. My brother writes down who they aren't.
The families are choosing their own names in the archive record. That's how it should have been from the start.
You look like people who need a boat and can't be seen asking for one.
Who are you?
Sak. Forger, some say. Logistics, I say. Passage out of Bellharbor, anywhere the tide goes.
Price: the customs house confiscated a ledger of mine. Get it back and you sail free.
What is in the ledger?
Names. Numbers. The usual paperwork of making people disappear, in a nice way.
'In a nice way.'
There's a nice way! I'll show you. Ledger first.
The clerk won't leave the counter unless something louder than her happens. Ask the kid with the pot.
Recover Sak's confiscated ledger from the customs house (south-west of the quay).
Customs. Closed. Unless you're filing a complaint, in which case also closed.
The clerk won't leave the counter. Something louder than her would have to happen outside.
The counter is empty.
Kid. How'd you like to be a hero of the harbour for exactly one minute?
Is it the pot?
It's the pot.
CLANG. CLANG. CLANG. Half the quay runs to the water's edge to see what the tide is doing.
Customs clerk will be out looking at the sea. Now or never. Well - now or in a few minutes.
Nobody past the counter.
...the tide's doing WHAT? Stay here. Don't touch anything.
Behind the counter: the confiscation shelf. A thick ledger, chain unlocked.
Hey! That's evidence!
Run. Back alleys. Follow me and don't be where the guards are standing.
(Being caught only sends you back to the alley mouth. The guards never leave their posts.)
Got you -
Not today. Back the way we came!
Lost them. Chartmaker lane. My brother's office. Don't tell him I ran.
Bring the ledger to Jori's office in Chartmaker Lane.
Jori is waiting outside his office. He takes the ledger and opens it without asking.
Seven barrels of lamp oil. Extremely talkative lamp oil.
Her name is Senn.
Not at the checkpoint it is not.
And when she asks for her wages?
We work something out.
You work something out. She waits.
Keep the names with the cargo numbers.
I did.
Then give them back.
A woman steps out of the lane. She has been listening.
Which name am I allowed to use?
...Whichever you want. That's - that should be yours.
Then write it down somewhere the ministry can't cross it out.
There's an archive under the tide. The drowned archive. Old contracts, older than the ministry. A record there isn't theirs.
I'll take you. I owe - I owe the paperwork.
Sak's Tricks include Pilfer: steal from enemies. The Journal keeps rumors you hear, separate from your objective.
Reach the Drowned Archive, south-east along the coast from Bellharbor, at low water.
Sak says the Drowned Archive opens its tide door at low water, south-east of Bellharbor.
The tide door stands open at low water. Salt light moves across drowned shelves.
Records nobody owns. Contracts older than the Crown. The ministry forgot this place because it couldn't tax it.
Three bells on the nave floor. Old archives opened by tone.
Open the Bell Nave's galleries by matching bell tones to their doors.
A low tone rolls through the nave. (ANCHOR glyph.) The west door hums.
A middle tone, clear as water. (WAVE glyph.) The east door hums.
A high tone rings bright. (LANTERN glyph.) Somewhere deeper, past the dry gallery, a door answers.
The anchor door stays shut. (It answers to the low tone - ring the west bell.)
The anchor door slides back into the wall.
The wave door stays shut. (It answers to the middle tone - ring the north bell.)
The wave door lifts, and seawater sighs in over the threshold.
The lantern door stays shut. (It answers to the high tone - the east bell in the nave.)
The lantern door opens onto the Witness Vault.
A figure of salt and bronze rises from the vault floor. Three bells hang from its shoulders.
UNREGISTERED READERS. THE ARCHIVE IS SEALED.
Registered, unregistered. Everyone always wants a form.
When one bell vibrates, it mirrors the last element used. Change elements - or use steel.
The Custodian settles back into the floor, its bells silent. The shelves around the vault stay open.
Don't close it again. Please. I've been trying to reach this vault for two years.
Who are you?
Elian Rook. Ministry geologist, until I wrote the wrong report. I study heartglass.
The organs are not fossils. They are transmitting. Continuously. A distributed consciousness spread across every relay in the kingdom.
I don't ask you to believe me. I have names, dates, and the transmission logs. Read them.

Relay transmission logs, 312 years of samples. The pulse is not random: it repeats, it answers, it forms patterns that change when names are spoken near it. Extraction increases output and suffering-analogous distortion together. Appendix: seven relay sites. Appendix page 9 missing.
Page nine is missing.
Water damage.
The pages on either side are dry.
...Water damage.
Speak with Rook in the Witness Vault.
There is a last synchronization chamber, under the Crown Dais in Veyr. If the relays could be released from there -
We investigate. Nothing more until we understand it.
Investigate. Yes. Of course.
The Roof Pier is north of the vault.
The roof pier. The tide is turning. From the harbor, a bell rings - a real bell, rehung by the town.
They're copying the evidence. Every family in Bellharbor is taking a page home.
You can't burn a thousand copies.
You can ignore them.
Not if we act.
We're going to see the chamber. That's all.
Rook agrees quickly. Too quickly, Elowen thinks. She doesn't say so yet.
Something long and gentle rises under the pier: a serpent-shaped Vestige, humming the harbor bell's note.
You rang the old bells and did not seal the doors again. I will answer your call.
The Pale Basin holds the memory vaults. That's where the relays remember what they were. The route north is the Skychain.
Take the coastal ferry north to Skyspine (east pier on the world road), then the Skychain Viaduct.
Sailors say the Skychain's anchors failed; High Aerie is sending a volunteer to reset them alone.
Maintenance crew, Skychain anchors. We'd reset them ourselves if the captain let us up.
Captain says it's a one-person job. Captain's sister volunteered. Of course she did.
Travellers. The Skychain's closed. Anchors failed in the last storm.
I'm going up alone to reset them. One leap from the high anchor to the nest, a few turns of the capstan, and the span holds.
And if you miss the leap?
Then High Aerie adds a name to the memorial and sends the next one. It's an honourable way to fall.
There's room on those anchors for a whole maintenance crew. Why is it a one-person job?
...Because it always has been.
We're crossing anyway. Come with us. Bring the crew.
The ballast yard locks steady the wind lanes. The crew knows the locks.
Fine. We go together. I'll still take the nest myself.
We'll see.
Vespera's Aerial techniques leave the field and strike on landing. While airborne she can't be targeted.
Cross the Skychain: lock the ballast in the yard, then cross the span to the Chain Nest.
The first ballast lock drops into place. Across the span, the west half of the middle lane goes still.
The ballast lock is set.
The second lock seats with a groan of chain. The east half of the middle lane calms.
The ballast lock is set.
The Chain Nest. A great grey bird is chained to the anchor ring, its wings holding the whole span level.
The Chain Roc. They tethered it here as a stabiliser. It's been holding the bridge up for years.
A living anchor. Of course it is. Everything here is somebody's body holding something up.
If I cut the tether mid-leap, the span drops. If I don't, it keeps screaming.
Or the crew holds the alternate cable while you cut. Like we discussed. Like adults.
The Roc strains against its chain. A shadow sweeps across the front row.
The Roc slumps against the anchor, exhausted. The crew's alternate cable is already rigged, taut and steady.
...The span's holding.
Because six people are holding it. Cut the tether.
Vespera cuts the chain. The Roc beats its wings once, twice, and lifts away into the cloud. Nobody falls.
I was supposed to - there was supposed to be a leap.
You survived something you expected to die for. That can be disorienting.
Continue to the High Landing, north-east of the nest.
The High Landing. The crew is already bolting the new anchors into the rock, cheering in bursts.
They're going to want to put me on a wall.
Which wall?
The memorial. For nearly dying.
You didn't nearly die. You did a maintenance shift.
...I don't know how to be thanked for that.
High Aerie's cable ferry now runs west across the chasm toward the Pale Basin and Nacre.
Visit High Aerie (north), then take the cable ferry west to the Pale Basin.
Vespera says the wind shrine above High Aerie's stair is older than the Crown.
At the wind shrine the cloths stream east. Something winged and fierce dives out of the cloud: a griffon of storm and sky.
The Roc is free. It hunted me from this shrine for years, chained. I was never the anchor. You unchained the anchor.
I will ride your wind when you call.
Captain Edda Hale. Vespera's sister and supervisor. The Skychain's closed until the anchors are reset.
The evidence from the vault - Vespera told me. The cable ferry runs on a relay under the court. If that relay goes silent, every basket stops mid-chasm.
I need transit that doesn't depend on something screaming under my feet. Can your machinist do anything?
The cable brake by the operator's post. If I give it a counterweight governor, the baskets hold without the relay.
You brought my sister back with a crew behind him. I don't have a ceremony for that. I should.
Forty years flying rescue baskets. I'll tell you a secret: the ceremonial uniforms make safe landings harder.
All that cloth. Looks grand falling. Snags on everything landing.
Cable ferry's stopped until the Skychain anchors are sorted.
Cable ferry's running west to the basin. Board at the chasm edge on the world road, west of the court.
When I grow up I'm going to fall off something really high. For the wall.
Or you could fly rescue and come home for supper.
...Can I do both?
No.
My son is on the memorial. I'd trade the wall for one more supper.
We practise the heroic leap every morning. We never practise the landing.
Returners' hall. Beds for crews coming back from the cliffs. Most nights, there's room.
Stop. I'm alone and I'm not armed for you. Crimson Oni, binding officer. Until this morning.
You wrote the warrants.
I wrote the seals. The warrants were written above me. That distinction won't matter to you and it shouldn't.
The prisoners inside are bound by my seals. I can walk you to them. In return, safe conduct out of the Basin.
No. We will not trade one set of prisoners for another bargain. We go in to free them properly.
Properly?
Each seal is keyed to a warrant number. Replace it with a key the person inside actually gives us. Their name. Their consent.
...That's slower.
Yes.
Fine. I'll show you the Names Hall. You won't like how little is written there.
(The Barracks lead north to the Names Hall and east to the Binding Cells. Read each seal; ask each prisoner.)
Record each prisoner's own consent key: read their seal in the Names Hall, ask them in the Binding Cells.
Seal 4471. A warrant number, a date, and in a smaller hand at the edge: 'Hallen - weaver.'
Seal 4471: Hallen, weaver.
Seal 4472. No name at all. Scratched into the stone beneath it: 'Ysa'.
Seal 4472: Ysa.
Seal 4473. 'Dragonborn, unit of the Cinder line.' Beside it, in chalk, a child's letters: 'CORVIN'.
Seal 4473: Corvin.
Hallen. I weave. Wove. Are you here to move me to another cell?
We're here to ask whether you want to leave. If you do, your name opens the lock.
...Yes. Hallen. I want to leave.
Hallen. I said yes. I'll keep saying it.
Thank you is too small. I'll find a bigger word later.
Don't open it yet. Not until you've asked the others. I won't be first out and leave them.
We'll ask each of them. What is your name?
Ysa. And yes. After them, or with them. Not before.
Ysa. Yes - with the others.
Together. Good.
They call me by the seal number. I've started calling myself by it too. That's the worst part.
The Names Hall says Corvin.
Someone wrote that? ...Corvin. Yes. That's me. Let me out.
Corvin. Say it again when you open it.
Corvin. Out loud. I'll get used to it.
The binding sigil dims. In its place, a new key glows with a single word: HALLEN. The door opens.
The seal is keyed to a warrant number. Read the name in the Names Hall first.
You have the name, but not the person's answer. Ask the one inside.
The cell is open.
YSA. The second door opens, after the first, as she asked.
Ysa asked to leave with the others, not before them.
The seal is keyed to a warrant number. Read the name in the Names Hall first.
You have the name, but not the person's answer. Ask the one inside.
The cell is open.
CORVIN. The last sigil gives way.
The seal is keyed to a warrant number. Read the name in the Names Hall first.
You have the name, but not the person's answer. Ask the one inside.
The cell is open.
That's my seal design you just replaced. I built it so no one could change the key without the warrant office.
You did it with a name and a question.
If I'm going to be useful: my blade takes an infusion - fire, ice or storm - and my runes strip what enemies are wearing. One infusion at a time.
Oni's Runes infuse his blade and unseal enemy protections. Formation lets you choose your active five at safe points.
Free all three prisoners, then face whatever holds the Tribunal Ring.
The Tribunal Ring. An ivory figure holds a warrant bearing Raven's description - and a ward seal meant for a dragonborn.
HOST LOCATED. TRANSFER OF WARD TO SUBJECT RAVEN. AUTHORISED BY OFFICER ONI.
Oni.
I authorised a transfer template. Years ago. I didn't know it would ever be you.
OFFICER ONI. APPLY YOUR SEAL. COMPLETE THE TRANSFER.
Oni raises his officer's seal. For a moment it could go either way. Then he breaks it across his knee.
Transfer refused.
Its sigil shows whether the next seal targets skills or strength. Alternate commands; Attack and Defend are never both locked.
The Adjudicator's ivory cracks into plain chalk. The ward template it carried dissolves with it.
The Snow Exit. The freed prisoners walk out first, blinking in the white.
You broke your seal instead of using it.
Yes.
That was useful. It's not forgiveness.
I know.
Nacre keeps a hearing house. Send your testimony there. Your name, in your own hand.
I will. And I'll come back to answer it. When this is done - whatever this is.
You'll travel with us until then.
Under that understanding. Yes.
Now the Memory Vault. North of Nacre. Everything the relays remember is kept there.
Go to Nacre (east of Whitebone), then north to the Memory Vault.
Archivist Sen. Nacre keeps disagreements. Other archives keep only the winner's copy.
The Memory Vault is north, up the vault road. Go in with a question, not an answer.
You kept both accounts. Good. The record is heavier than it was. That's how you know it's honest.
Do the plants count as sacred? No idea. They need water either way.
The pool showed my grandmother's wedding. My granddaughter saw a funeral in the same water.
We saw the same morning. It was both. We argue about it every week. It's our favourite argument.
Salt, jars, remedies. The good cloth-lined jars keep water sweet across the flats.
Water carried in cloth-lined jars. It tastes of linen. You get used to it.
I came to hear my mother in the pool. I heard three other people's mothers. It helped anyway.
Quiet cloister. We ask little and you rest long. No talking after the second bell.
Listening is a practice. You don't take from the pool. You let it tell you, and you're allowed to stop.
The listening pool. It holds voices that were never anyone's property. Come back later. It will still be here.
The Listening Gate. Words cut in the lintel: 'The vault will show you memory, if you consent. You may refuse. The walls carry the same testimony in ink.'
It is asking. That is more than the ministry ever did.
A cool pressure behind the eyes, then light. The vault will show you what it holds.
You decline. The gate dims politely. Ink testimony lines every wall ahead.
(Your choice changes how the vault presents its testimony, not what you learn.)
Gather the three testimonies and set them in order on the chronology wall in the Voluntary Accord.
312 years ago, a regional disaster. Some humans and dragons chose to share bodies to survive it. Each accord was voluntary. Each included a separation rite, available to either party at any time.
Memory: two voices in one throat, laughing about the weather. One of them says, 'Whenever you want to leave, say so.'
Testimony I: the voluntary accords, with a separation rite.
A regulator crew chief: 'They said the hosts were infrastructure now. We stopped using names on the shift boards. The separation rite was struck from the training manual.'
Testimony II, first account: the rite was removed; hosts became infrastructure.
A ministry order: 'Standardisation improves safety. Separation rites caused outages. Discontinuation is humane in aggregate.'
'Humane in aggregate.' That's a sentence you'd only write if you knew it was a lie.
Or if you believed it. Both accounts go in the record.
Testimony II, second account: the ministry's reasons for standardisation.

A century ago: the last independent great dragons were broken into distributed consciousnesses, spread across bred lineages and relay organs. The industry called the organs fossils. The lineages were called hosts.
Memory flickers toward a nursery ledger. Raven stops at the records and does not step into the named child's memory.
Records only. It's hers.

A century ago: the last independent great dragons were broken into distributed consciousnesses, spread across bred lineages and relay organs. The industry called the organs fossils. The lineages were called hosts.
Testimony III: engineered lineages and distributed consciousness.
The chronology wall has three slots. Which testimony goes first?
Second?
Third?
The wall accepts the record: voluntary accords; their standardisation, in two voices; the engineered lineages. The choir door beyond the galleries opens.
(A voice from far above, carried by the vault): Heavier than it was.
The Choir Chamber is open, north of the First Industry and the Quiet Nursery.
The wall rejects it. A record with one voice removed is not a record. The tablets return to their shelves.
Dissonance. The tablets slide back to their shelves. (The dates on each tablet show the order.)
The wall needs three testimonies, and both accounts of the second. (The Voluntary Accord, the First Industry, the Quiet Nursery.)
The chronology is set.
The Choir Chamber. Three masked figures sing one note so perfectly that it hurts to hear.
ONE HISTORY. ONE ACCOUNT. REMOVE THE CONTRADICTION.
It wants to make every account agree. Vary your commands - it echoes whatever you repeat.
The masks crack. The single note breaks into many voices, all different, none silenced.
A small fox made of warm light steps out of the broken chorus and sits at Aurex's feet.
You kept every voice. I light what is actually there. Call me when you need to see.
The Still Pool. Raven kneels at the water. His reflection moves a half-beat late.
There is enough of me here to begin again.
Here means my hands.
They made them to hold me.
They are still mine.
You would keep me imprisoned.
I would stop you calling my life an empty room.
There was a way to leave. Before they removed it.
Then we find that way.
And until then?
You ask.
...I am asking to speak with you. Not through you.
Yes.
So the heartglass organs are relays, and dragonborn are - memory nodes. Living ones.
And the relays can be released. All at once, from the Crown Dais.
'Released' would include every dragonborn host. Every node. At once.
Freedom for all of them.
Without asking any of them.
Return the evidence to Cinderwake, High Aerie and Nacre. Each needs something different.
The Golem and Aurex think a single relay could be released slowly, locally, without a captive holding it.
The old cooling channel under the garden. The Golem talks two crew members through fitting the bypass, plated arms folded.
Left valve first. No - your other left. Good. Now you know it and I don't have to.
Heat without the regulator. Slower to warm up. Doesn't hum.
(Cinderwake's guarantee: heat, maintained by its own crew.)
The cable brake by the operator's post. The Golem adds a counterweight governor while Vespera and the crew hold the basket steady.
The basket's hanging on its own weight now. No relay.
Good. Write down how you did it. Put it on a wall, since we love walls.
(High Aerie's guarantee: stable transit that doesn't depend on a relay.)
Nacre needs the hardest thing: a way to separate consent from pressure. Every dragonborn here has been told what to want by someone with a seal.
Hearings with no officer in the room. The person speaks, the record keeps it, nobody signs over them.
And the answer can change later. That is what the old separation rite understood.
Then we hold the first hearing tonight. One volunteer. One relay. No hurry.
(Nacre's guarantee: consent heard without institutional pressure.)
(Accord visits remaining: Cinderwake's garden bypass, High Aerie's cable brake, Nacre's hearing with Sen.)
All three communities agreed. Meet the volunteer at the trial relay by Nacre's listening pool.
I'm the first volunteer. When the three towns agree, we'll try the relay. Not before.
Everyone's here. Step up to the relay when you're ready.
A trial relay outside Nacre, humming in a stone housing. The Golem has built a distributed circuit around it; Aurex sits with the volunteer.
One relay. Kept alive, no captive holding it. The load goes out to the wheel, the cable, the pool - little bits, everywhere.
You may stop at any point. Say so, and we stop.
I know.
Slowly - over a long hour - the hum changes key. It doesn't stop. It stops sounding like someone holding their breath.
One relay. While a hundred keep screaming.
This one no longer needs a captive to hold it.
How many years will you ask them to wait?
Ask me.
You should not have to accept this.
I have not accepted it. I am choosing how to leave.
...I almost agreed with you, Rook. Almost.
The difference is not nothing.
It will be, to the ones who do not live long enough.
Rook leaves before anyone can answer. Elowen watches him go south.
He's heading for the old aqueduct under Veyr. The Conduit.
Voss has been massing soldiers at the Crown Dais for weeks. If Rook forces a synchronisation there -
Every node at once. Every dragonborn. Nobody asked.
One more thing. My plan of the Conduit shows three relay stations. The dais draws load for four. I can't find the fourth.
Then we watch for it.
Stop a forced mass awakening. Enter the Sable Conduit (old aqueduct north of Veyr).
The old aqueduct under Veyr. The water is gone; cable runs where it used to flow. Somewhere above, bells are ringing for a coronation nobody announced.
Eight of us, one tunnel. We can't all fight in a corridor this narrow.
Four in front, four behind carrying the lamps and watching the flank. We swap when someone is tired. Not when someone is spent.
Voss has three relay stations feeding the dais. South relay, north lift relay, and the bridge itself.
And the lifts. The evacuation lifts run on a separate feed. Whatever we cut, we don't cut those.
There are people in those lifts. Ministry clerks, conscripts, families from the lower wards. Voss called it 'relocation'.
(Everyone travels together. Choose your active five with Formation in the menu at any time outside battle.)
Release the south relay (west) and reroute the north lift relay (east) without cutting lift power.
Lift's still running. Whatever you're doing down there, keep doing it that way.
Both relays quiet and the lift never dropped. I've been doing this nineteen years. First time anyone asked me before touching the feed.
A synchronization relay, singing the coronation note. Its housing matches the trial relay at Nacre.
Same trick as the trial. Spread the load, don't slam it off.
And stop if it answers no.
Morwen's hand is on the housing before anyone else moves - then she stops.
No. If it's somebody in there, I'm not doing to them what Rook wants to do to everyone.
(The relay is still singing. Try the slow release.)
The note bends, then settles, then goes out like a lamp being turned down rather than blown. Somewhere far above, one bell misses its beat.
South relay is resting. It will wake if somebody asks it to.
South relay released. Reroute the north lift relay (east from the aqueduct), then head north to the Soldiers' Walk.
The south relay is dim and quiet.
The lift stopped between floors, then came down here. They said the ministry needs the power. We're not going anywhere until someone turns the lift back on.
It moved! It's taking the next group up to the river gate. Thank you - whoever you are.
The north relay feeds both the dais line and the occupied lift. A lever can switch the lift to the old aqueduct feed.
Lift first. Then the relay. The other order drops a car full of people.

options.text: Switch the lift to the aqueduct feed, then quiet the relay

cmds.text: The lift lights flicker as the load wavers. You stop at once. The lift holds - barely. (Lift first.)
The lift cable shudders, catches the old feed, and starts to climb. Only then does the relay go dark.
That's the ministry's own lift, carrying the ministry's own clerks out. Nobody's going to write that down.
I will.
North relay rerouted. Go north to the Soldiers' Walk.
The north relay is dark. The lift runs on the aqueduct feed.
Don't - we're not fighting. The ceiling came down on the barracks when the bells started. Three of us are pinned.
It takes all of you and a borrowed crowbar. Nobody is badly hurt.
Voss told us the dais would 'end the instability'. He didn't say what he meant by it.
Take this. Field kit. We're going up with the lift.
...We'll be here.
We'll get the others moving to the lift. If you see the Marshal - he isn't going to stop.
Beyond the Soldiers' Walk the corridor opens onto the Marshal Bridge. Past it, the Crown Dais.
Listen. Whatever happens past this door, some of it will not be undone.
Then we write down where we were before it.
(A protected backup has been written: "Before the Crown Dais". It is separate from your save slots and can be loaded from Load at any time.)
(This is the last point where you can freely leave the Conduit. Rest and save at the lamp if you need to.)
Cross the Marshal Bridge (north) and stop Voss before he takes the network.
Stop there. You are standing on the only bridge that holds this country together.
You're holding it together with people's names, Marshal.
I am replacing a hundred unstable relays with one stable authority. No more outages. No more hosts deciding they would rather not.
That last part is the point for you. Not the outages.
Order is a kindness to people who cannot afford chaos.
You signed my forgeries' death certificates yourself, sir. Twice. I checked.
Then you know I read everything I sign. Guards - protect the Marshal.
Voss raises the command baton and points at a protector.
Voss staggers back against the bridge relay. The baton cracks.
You think you have won something. Rook is already at the dais. He does not need my authority. He wants none at all.
Voss retreats into the central apparatus below the bridge. The hatch seals behind him.
Let him go. Rook first.
The bridge relay is exposed now. Quiet it and the dais door opens.
Quiet the bridge relay, then climb to the Crown Dais.
The bridge relay. The third synchronization line.
The Golem and Aurex release it the way they did in Nacre. It goes dim. The dais door groans open.
Three visible relays. All dark.
Visible.
Climb to the Crown Dais.
The bridge relay is dark.
You came. Good. I wanted witnesses who had read the vault.
We read it. It said the separation rite was taken away. Not that you get to hand it back to everyone at once.
A century of extraction, and you want to repair it one volunteer at a time.
One volunteer at a time is how you know they're volunteers.
And the ones who die waiting? Do they get a hearing?
They get asked. That is what you are skipping.
Then I will be the one who didn't ask. Someone has to.
Three relay lights kindle around the dais.
Rook goes down on one knee. The dais controls spark and fail. The Golem pulls the last visible coupling.
The visible relays are dark.
Then why is it still climbing?
Rook.
I could not leave it to permission.
Whose permission?
Any of yours.
Under the dais floor, lines the Golem never drew light one after another - the fourth relay, the pasted-over line from the archive diagram.
(Through Raven's throat, a command arrives that is not his own: overwrite the host.)
No.
Was that for him or for me?
For the command.
The common channel - it's giving every node the same order. I can break it. Not stop it. Break it.
The lifts still have power. Move.
Aurex sets both hands on the dais and pulls the channel apart. The order shatters into a thousand small voices. It does not stop.
...It was supposed to be freedom.
It was supposed to be asked.
Soldiers drag Rook toward the lift. Nobody lets go of him, and nobody leaves him behind.
Escape! Reach the evacuation lift at the end of the collapsing aqueduct.
Stone rains down in waves. Wait for the shaking to pass, then run.
The lift cage slams shut. The Golem throws every lever he built into the cable brake.
Holding - holding -
The Conduit gives way beneath Veyr.
Coastlines fracture along old relay faults. Dormant dragon structures rise from the plains and the sea. The Crown's bell rings once, wrong, and every city hears it.
The lift cable snaps. The party scatters into the dark.
Salt water. A fire, somewhere. Someone humming badly.
A cot on a floating pontoon. A fire in an iron drum. Someone is humming, badly.
Don't sit up yet. You swallowed half the Ember Sea.
The Ember - what sea?
The one that used to be the middle of the country. Three weeks ago.
The others?
Scattered. I have been having visions - pieces of them. They are not reliable. I am not reliable right now either.
So we do the reliable things first. Eat. Help. Listen.
Mara Pell. Brackenford, until the river moved. Now I run a floating town, apparently.
You can pay for your cot the way everyone does. The lamps need fuel carried, and the east walkway's broken.
Help at Hearthward: carry lamp fuel for the keeper, fix the broken walkway, and ask about the others.
The lamp keeper needs fuel from the plank pile crates. And the east walkway is out.
Fuel cans and planks. Take what you can carry. Everyone carries something here.
(You pick up two cans of lamp fuel and a length of plank.)
Lamps first, then planks. Keeper's by the hearth.
Fuel! Bless you. The night lamps go on the outer pontoons so the fishing skiffs can find home.
You've got a plank, too. The east walkway broke yesterday. There's a family stuck on the far pontoon.
Sit with Aurex by the hearth.
The lamps are low. There's fuel in the crates by the plank pile - if you can carry some over, the skiffs will thank you.
Lamps are lit. Nobody's lost on the water tonight.
We're fine! We just can't get across. Somebody said there were planks.
Thank you. The kids were starting to think this pontoon was a new country.
Raven lays the plank across the gap and Aurex lashes it down. It isn't pretty. It holds.
Oh thank goodness. Come on, kids - dry land. Well. Dry pontoon.
Walkway fixed. Carry the lamp fuel to the keeper by the hearth.
Sit with Aurex by the hearth.
A gap in the walkway. You'd need a plank - there's a pile by the cots.
The patched walkway creaks, but holds.
Fish broth. Every day. Tomorrow I'm told there may be a potato.
The old woman in the corner cot keeps asking for her husband by his quarry number. I keep answering with his name.
Cots, blankets, a fire. That's the whole inn. Nobody's charged; everyone helps.
A salvage chest. Things found floating, washed up, or dragged out of the sealed ruins are brought here for their owners.
(The chest is empty for now.)
The lamps are lit. The walkway holds. Aurex and Raven sit by the hearth drum.
Would the world be safer without me in it? Without - us.
No. I refuse the premise. Your body is not a public utility, Raven. Not the ministry's, not Rook's, not the world's.
I heard them. During the activation. Other fragments, taking their hosts' voices. Some hosts let them. Some did not get the choice.
Then we free both. The fragments and the hosts. Without making either of them disposable.
Both.
News, since you're awake. A signal flare's been going up over the flooded Rootward every dusk. Three green, one red. Old guide code.
Elowen.
Brackenford's west of here along the pontoon road. Rootward's north of it, where the forest used to be dry.
And take the supplies in the hearth chest. You two can't fight the whole sea with borrowed spoons.
Follow Elowen's signal flares to the flooded Rootward (north-west, past Brackenford).
Brackenford's bakery is a footbridge depot now. Mara says the bunkhouse became a shelter.
Help first, then talk. That's how Hearthward works.
Every tent that becomes a cabin, somebody argues about which one gets the roof first. Good. Arguing means we expect to still be here.
The Ash Accord. I never thought I'd see ministry clerks and quarry crews sign the same page.
People bring the signs from their old shops. Not the palace banners - the bakeries, the cobblers, the laundries.
Nobody fished out a throne. Nobody wanted to.
Roofs first! The rain's coming.
Water first! You can't drink a roof.
...Fine. Water tanks, then roofs.
And we write it down, so we don't have this argument again tomorrow.
The bell rang wrong. Everyone says so. I think it rang right and everything else went wrong.
Fuel for the lamps is in the crates by the plank pile at the hearth.
Lamps stay lit every night now. We rotate who carries.
Ponton market. Whatever floats, whatever's found, whatever's traded.
Ferry to the Glass Coast? Hull's cracked. When someone clears the Rootward current, I'll have my caulk back.

options.text: Take the repaired ferry east to Bellharbor

cmds.text: The ferry creeps across the Ember Sea, past dragon spines rising from the water, to what's left of Bellharbor's upper town.
Empty berth. The Rune Golem had plans for a ship here - a rescue ship. Heard he's in Cinderwake, if anyone's alive there.
Wayfarer. Slowest ship I ever saw. Also the only one.
Wayfarer's tender runs from the end of the berth. Step on and we'll row you up.
A camp on the high roots. Tarps, a cook fire, and forty people who have been waiting for the water to decide something.
Raven? Aurex. You're alive. Good. Don't touch the map.
Hello to you too.
There are three crossings north of here. Two of them drown people. One doesn't. I know which. So I lead every group across myself.
How many trips a day?
As many as it takes.
Which is why half of them are still here after two weeks. Nobody can wait for one guide forever, Elowen.
If I hand out the map and somebody takes the wrong crossing -
Then we make every crossing the right one.
...The current's being pushed south by something in the old sluice. If the sluice lets go, the water drops. The walkways can be raised with the levers - if you know which way they lift.
Raise all three walkways in the Three Crossings (north), then find what is diverting the current.
Who's that? Oh - it's you.
Three levers, three walkways. Up is up - don't overthink it. The thing in the sluice is another story.
She's been carrying the whole camp on one map. Let's give her arms a rest.
Elowen says the forest used to be dry. I don't believe her. Trees can't live without swimming.
My hip won't take the ford twice. I'll go once, on a proper walkway, or not at all.
The west lever lifts. A walkway rises dripping out of the flood, planks still marked with old guild paint.
The west walkway is raised.
The middle lever groans. The centre walkway surfaces, green with weed.
The middle walkway is raised.
The east lever snaps up. The last walkway rises, and for a moment the whole pool is quiet.
The east walkway is raised.
(The current still tugs at the lowered crossings.)
All three crossings are up. Follow the current north to the old sluice.
The old sluice. A shape of bark and silt and drowned iron is holding the gate shut with its whole body, forcing the river south over the camp.
It thinks it's holding back the flood. It is the flood.
The Warden turns. Water surges toward the front row.
The Warden sinks, and the sluice gate swings free. The water level drops a hand's width, then another.
You did it. The current's falling.
Now the map.
...There's only one. It took me four years.
Then it's the most valuable thing in the camp, and it belongs to the camp.
If someone reads it wrong -
Then they ask someone who read it right. That is how maps work when more than one person owns them.
Fine. We make copies. One per family. Warnings in the margins. Names of who keeps each crossing.
It's a start. Not a finish. I'm not done paying for what I sold, back before any of this.
Come with us?
Someone's got to find Morwen. She never could read a map.
Brackenford's new crossings are open. Take the repaired ferry from Hearthward east to Bellharbor to find Morwen.
Hearthward's ferryman has his caulk back. The ferry to the Glass Coast runs again.
I split my days between here and Hearthward. We count the shelter by name every night - that part I won't hand to anyone.
New crossings, copies of Elowen's map on every door. Brackenford's two halves talk again.
The bunkhouse is a shelter now. Forty cots. The forewoman counts us by name every night. Nobody's a number in here.
A cot and a bowl. Nobody's charged.
The bakery's a footbridge depot. Bread in the morning, planks in the afternoon, and I still burn the rye.
The west camp wants the road to the mill first. The east camp wants the road to the clinic. We'll see.
Clinic road first. Grain's no good to a man with a fever.
I kept extending credit after the quarry stopped paying. Now there's no quarry and no pay. I'm still extending it. Somebody has to believe in tomorrow.
Salvage crew. Anything we pull out of the sealed ruins goes to Hearthward's salvage chest - with the owner's name, if we can find it.
The upper gallery of the old archive annex. The roof sags over a shelter of families - held up by a lattice of white light.
Beneath it, standing in knee-deep water, Morwen. Her hands are raised. They are shaking.
Morwen!
Don't come under the edge. The roof goes when I stop.
She's been holding it for three days. We bring her water. She won't sit.
Then we get everyone out from under it first. The walkway above - is it passable?
Bales came down across it in the first quake. There are winches, but nobody's had the hands.
Clear the upper walkway with the two winches (west side passage), then lead the three families out along it.
Not yet. There are still people under here. Don't ask me to stop.
...Is that everyone?
Kids are ringing the alarm with a cooking pot since the ministry took the bells. Loudest thing in town.
The winch creaks. The first mass of rope-bales lifts off the walkway and swings clear.
The west winch is holding the bales clear.
The second winch lifts the last bales. The walkway runs clear to the east stair.
The east winch is holding the bales clear.
The walkway's blocked. We tried. We'll wait for the young woman to finish whatever she's doing.
Up the gap and along the walkway? At my age? ...Yes. Yes, all right. Take my arm.
We can't go through the water - my son can't swim. And the walkway's full of bales.
The walkway's clear? Then we're going. Thank you. Thank her.
I'm not scared. I'm waiting. It's different.
Is the lady going to be okay? ...Okay. I'll go if you count me.
One. There. You are counted.
(Some families are still under the roof.)
Everyone is out along the walkway. Go to Morwen.
The roof goes when I stop.
Nobody is under it now.
There could be -
We counted them. Twice.
Let it go.
I do not know what happens after.
We light the lamps.
Morwen lowers her hands. The lattice goes out. The roof comes down into empty water with a long, tired sound.
Darkness. Then, one by one along the walkway, ordinary lanterns - held by the families she was protecting.
They did that. Not me.
You can sit down now, Morwen.
I can sit down.
The Golem. We have to find the Golem. I want to see a machine that runs without someone pretending to be its fuel.
Travel to Cinderwake (north-west, beyond Rootward) and find the Golem.
Cinderwake crews are rotating heat between workshops with waterwheels. Someone says the Golem is in the old assembly yard.
Morwen's in the upper gallery. She won't let go of the roof. Please - she'll listen to you before she listens to me.
The lower streets are gone, but the ropewalks make good roads. We're painting names on every door that has someone behind it.
Sak - if you see him - tell him I have people who need their names fixed. The right way this time.
CLANG! That's the alarm. They took the bells so I use the pot. CLANG! That one was for practice.
The tide chapel is an evacuation station now. We ring for boats, not for prayers. Both get answered about as often.
Charts! Old charts, useless. New charts, useful but wrong. Buy both and average them.
The ropewalks were for making rope. Now they're the only roads above water. Rope's still useful, mind.
Manifests used to list refugees as 'cargo'. Now we list cargo as 'refugees' so nobody steals it. Joke. Mostly.
Hammocks in the chapel loft. Free for anyone who pulls a shift on the pumps. You look like you'd pull a shift.
The old assembly yard. On the slipway lies a hull - broad, ugly, bolted rather than grown. The Golem is under it with a lamp.
Morwen. Elowen. Raven. Aurex. ...You're here. You're here and I'm leaking oil everywhere.
You found a ship.
I found a ship nobody finished. Rescue vessel, drafted before heartglass made everything 'efficient'. Steam and gears. Heavy. Slow.
Her name's Lanternwake. The engine works. I've tested every part twice. It just needs the cooling channels powered and room to fit the stabilisers.
And?
And the hull twists on the slipway. Nothing I've got is heavy enough to hold her straight while we bolt the keel.
Power the three cooling channels (valves on the north wall), then help the crews clear the assembly space.
Three valves on the north wall. The channels have to run cold before the engine can breathe.
Channels are cold! Now the crews can shift the scrap - talk to the crew chief.
Space is clear. Now all we need is something that can hold a ship straight. Something very heavy and very patient.
The west valve opens. Water hisses into the channel; the pipe frosts white.
The west channel runs cold.
The middle valve opens with a shudder. The channel under the slipway starts to sing.
The middle channel runs cold.
The east valve opens. Steam coils out of the vents and thins to nothing.
The east channel runs cold.
The channels are cold. Talk to the crew chief about clearing the assembly space.
Channels are running cold - we can work the yard now. Scrap on both sides, and a few rust-crawlers nesting in it.
You handle the crawlers, we handle the scrap. Deal?
The crews haul, stack and sort for an hour. The assembly space opens up around the hull.
Space is clear. Now - what's that at the east end? It wasn't there this morning.
Something very large is waiting at the east end of the slipway.
A tortoise the size of a cottage, its shell plated like a boiler. It has been watching the hull for some time.
I held up this yard's roof in the old days. Under orders. They called me a foundation.
Nobody has ordered me since the bell. So I came to see whether anyone would ask.
...Would you hold the hull straight while we bolt the keel? You can stop whenever you like. We'll brace it with jacks as we go, so it doesn't depend on you.
You asked. And you built it so it does not need me.
Then I will help. And afterward I will go where I like - which is, I think, with you.
The Iron Tortoise leans its shell against the hull. The crews bolt the keel in one long afternoon, jacks going in behind every bolt.
...Now the manual. Pell's going to ask.
Golem. Before you take her anywhere. The manual.
It's in my head.
That's the problem. Write it down. All of it. Every valve, every spare, every noise she makes when she's sick.
That's weeks of work -
Then we'll wait weeks. I'm not watching another machine that only works when one engineer stands beside it.
...You're right. You were right about the wheel, too.
The Golem writes for three days. Morwen checks every page. The crews read it aloud and argue with it, and the Golem changes it where they're right.
The manual lies on the workshop bench, heavy and dog-eared. Anyone can pick it up.
A workbench covered in the Golem's calculations. Very little of it is legible to anyone but the Golem.
The workbench, waiting for a manual.
The Lanternwake manual, dog-eared, with a pencil tied to it on a string. The newest note, in a crew hand: 'Page 12 is wrong. Fixed.'
Launch morning. The crews take their places - not the Golem. The Golem stands at the back, plated hands folded, runes dimmed.
Page one. Cooling channels open.
Open.
Page two. Boiler to working pressure. Slow.
Slow. Holding.
Page three. Release the slipway brakes.
Lanternwake slides down the slipway and lifts, heavy and steady, into the smoky sky over Cinderwake.
...I didn't touch anything.
You wrote it down. That's touching everything.
Lanternwake waits at Hearthward's berth. Find Vespera (High Aerie), Sak (Veyr) and Oni (Whitebone) - in any order.
High Aerie's broken chain now links two new islands. A cliff settlement there is evacuating.
Veyr's throne square is a distribution point. Someone is guarding the lower registry from Voss's remnants.
Whitebone's old cells are a sanctuary now. People with bindings nobody can safely remove shelter there.
Power fails in patches now. We rotate heat workshop by workshop. The clinic never goes cold - that's the one rule.
The Golem's in the old assembly yard east of here. He says he found a ship. He also says he's fine. He's lying about one of those.
The manual's on every bench in town now. People argue with it in the margins. That's how you know it's alive.
Heat rota: canteen at dawn, clinic always, workshops by turn. We post it on the wall under the injury tally.
The clinic's warm. That was the question you all asked, back when. Here's the answer: we share.
The tally wall. We kept counting after the bell. Fewer marks since the regulators went dark. Make of that what you like.
The pipes don't sing anymore. The waterwheels squeak instead. I like the squeak better.
Waterwheels at every terrace. Slower than the regulators. Nobody's inside them.
Shift stew. Same as ever. Except now there's a waterwheel keeping it warm instead of a - well. You know.
Cots by the canteen stove. Take a shift on the wheels if you want. Or don't. Rest.
The Skyspine chain has snapped. What's left of it links two new islands - and between them hangs a mooring, groaning, holding a cargo platform full of evacuees from the cliff settlement.
You're Vespera's lot. She's on the mooring lever. She's been on it all night.
Her plan is to cut herself loose with the load if it slips. Take the platform down with her, drop the weight, save the rest.
That's not a plan. That's a eulogy.
There are three ballast anchors - one on the settlement, one on the old anchor rock, one on the mooring island itself. Set all three and the mooring holds without anyone on it.
My crew can't cross the gust lanes carrying the ballast. Can you?
Set all three ballast anchors (north-west rock, settlement, mooring island). Cross the gust lanes between gusts.
Wind's the same as it ever was. Pennants lift, then the gust. You'll learn it in three crossings or you'll learn it in six.
We're waiting for the platform. Nobody's going to jump. Captain Hale said so.
Three anchors. You can't count on her counting them for you.
All three are set. Go and talk to my sister.
The ballast drops into the old anchor socket with a boom that rolls across the gap. The mooring line stops shivering quite so hard.
The north-west anchor is set.
The settlement anchor bites into the cliff. The evacuees cheer, then look embarrassed about cheering.
The settlement anchor is set.
The mooring island anchor clamps home. The platform steadies on its line.
The mooring anchor is set.
(The mooring still leans on the lever. Set the remaining anchors.)
All three anchors are set. Talk to Vespera at the mooring lever.
You came. Don't distract me. If this slips I've got about a second to cut.
The line's steady.
Three anchors are holding it. You can let go of the lever.
If I let go and I'm wrong -
Then the anchors are wrong, and we'll all be wrong together. Step away, Vespera.
Vespera takes her hands off the lever. One finger at a time. The mooring holds.
The platform comes across, and the evacuees walk off it onto solid rock.
I'm not putting your name on the memorial.
I didn't -
I'm putting it on the rescue roster. Tuesday shift. Don't be late.
...Tuesday.
I've already forged you a very convincing shift badge. Joke. Mostly.
Rescue roster. Write your own name on it. Nobody else should.
Vespera is back. Skyspine's anchor is ready for the release protocol.
My sister's on the mooring at the broken chain, south of here. Please bring her back with her hands empty.
Tuesday shift. She was early.
Windmills now instead of the hanging engines. They turn slower. They also don't scream.
