Every windmill has a crew name painted on its vane. That was the kid's idea.
I'm going to fly rescue baskets and come home for supper. Every day. That's the plan.
Cable court traders. Half the cables are gone, so we're 'court traders' now.
I came down on a rescue basket last winter. The pilot's not on any wall. I want her to be.
Returners' hall. There's always room.
A clean stretch of stone beside the memorial, waiting for something.
The Returners' Wall. Names of people who brought others home - pilots, basket crews, a cook who ran soup across the span in a gale. And an incident archive, open to anyone.
(Still missing: Vespera, at the broken Skyspine chain.)
(Still missing: Sak, under Veyr's registry.)
(Still missing: Oni, at the Whitebone sanctuary.)
Everyone is together again. Take the evidence to Nacre's assembly for the Ash Accord.
Nacre is gathering every town's delegates by the listening pool.
You came through Bellharbor? Then you know I've been trying to reach Sak. He's under the square, in the lower registry.
Voss's remnants want the ledgers - the ones that prove what they did. Sak won't let them near. He won't let anyone near, including the people whose names are in there.
The canals changed when the walls fell. The ladder by the south of the square goes down; the lock gates raise the crossings.
Reach the lower registry through Veyr's changed canals (ladder, south of the square).
Go on. I'll bring the satchel when it's time.
The west lock gate rises. Water drops in the west channel, and a crossing shoulders up out of it.
The west crossing is up.
The middle gate grinds open. The centre crossing surfaces, streaming.
The middle crossing is up.
The east gate lifts. The last crossing rises toward the registry stair.
The east crossing is up.
Uniforms at the registry door, stripped of rank but not of habit. Voss's remnants.
The ledgers are ministry property. Stand aside.
The ministry sank. The names didn't.
The remnants scatter back into the canals. Behind a barricade of filing cabinets, someone coughs.
Don't - oh. Oh, it's you. It's actually you.
And Vespera! Alive! Nobody told me you could survive falling off a sky.
I've been guarding the originals. Every forged pass I ever made is in here, next to the real name it replaced.
If the remnants get these, they burn them. If the refugees get them, they - I don't know what they'll do. That's what scares me.
That's not yours to decide, Sak.
I made the forgeries. Doesn't that make it mine to fix?
It makes it yours to answer for. Not to decide.
Bring the original ledgers to the residents at the tables and let them choose how their names are recorded.
New seal, blank forms, no forgeries. It's a very boring satchel now. I love it.
The original ledgers, stacked on the tables. Sak hovers.
This one's mine. Page forty. That's the name the ministry gave me when they sold my contract.
And here's the name my mother gave me. Different page.
I can write whichever you -
No. We decide how it's written. You can hold the ink.
The residents take the ledgers one page at a time. Some keep the old names. Some write new ones. Each entry is signed by the person it belongs to.
Sak.
Jori sets a worn leather satchel on the table - the one Sak used to carry false papers.
It's got blank forms in it now. And a proper seal, issued by the refugee assembly. It's yours, if you'll carry it.
...I'm not forgiven.
No. You're employed.
That's better. That's so much better.
You and I signed the same kind of papers, Sak. Different hands. Same ink.
...Then we both keep better ones now.
Sak is back. Veyr's distribution point is open.
The ledgers are behind the barricade. Someone is guarding them.
The ledgers, every entry signed by the person it names.
We've been waiting for our own names. Not for someone to hand them to us.
Page forty. My name. My handwriting. Nobody else's.
Registry's open for amendments. Every change is signed by the one who asked for it.
Clerk Ansel. I refused false death certificates back when it could get me hanged. Now I sign ration chits. Better job.
Do you think our families can eat loyalty?
Not anymore. They can eat the rations, though. So we hand out rations.
Distribution point. One line, no ranks. You'd be amazed how much faster it goes without ranks.
The throne used to be right there. Now it's a soup table. Nobody misses the throne.
South market, moved north because the south is underwater. Same prices. Mostly.
Barracks cots. Ex-barracks. Ex-cots, some of them, but they hold.
Whitebone's snow gate. The redoubt's cells are a sanctuary now - doors propped open, blankets on the bunks. Except three.
Oni?
Here. Don't come in with weapons out. Some of them flinch.
Three people still wear bindings I wrote. I can't take them off alone. If I get the key wrong, the seal repeats its command. I won't risk that on someone else's body.
I've already sent my name and testimony to Nacre. Whatever they decide, I'll answer it. But first - these three.
Open the three sealed cells one by one. Ask each person for their own consent key, then use it at their lock.
The sanctuary keeps no records of who is 'guilty'. Only who needs a blanket.
You're with him? ...I'll watch. That's all.
Ask them. Not me. I only know the command I wrote. They know who they are.
That's all three. I - thank you. No. That's not for me to say.
You want my key? It was a number, once. Warrant 4-11.
...My name is Hesk. That's the key. Hesk. Say it right.
Hesk. Go on. The lock's outside.
Seventy years I've had this seal. I'm not sure I remember my own name.
Then choose one. It doesn't have to be old to be yours.
...Wren. Old woman, new name. Wren.
Wren. I like how it sounds in someone else's mouth when they ask.
I don't want it off yet.
Then it stays on until you do.
...That's the first time anyone's said that. All right. Now. Key's 'Tamsin'. Now.
Tamsin. Quickly, before I change my mind. Or don't - I'm allowed to change it.
The seal hears 'Hesk', spoken the way he asked, and lets go. The cell door swings wide.
The lock waits for a key. Only the person inside can give it.
The cell is open.
'Wren.' The seal hesitates, as if surprised to hear a name it has never known, then releases.
The lock waits for a key. Only the person inside can give it.
The cell is open.
'Tamsin.' The binding unwinds. The door opens. Tamsin stays inside for a moment, then walks out on her own.
The lock waits for a key. Only the person inside can give it.
The cell is open.
All three cells are open. Walk Oni out to the sanctuary exit.
You wrote my number.
Yes.
You remember it.
Yes.
Do you know my name?
Not yet.
Then start there.
May I write it down?
...Ilse. With an s.
Oni writes it. The survivor watches him do it, and does not say thank you, and walks away.
Before I go back to Nacre for the hearing - Voss's network. If there's any way to stop it from compelling anyone again, I want to help.
The survivors decide that.
In the sanctuary hall, the survivors talk it over without him. They come back with a single page: a limited agreement. He may help. They keep a copy of his account.
You let someone else hold the lever. Took me years to learn that.
Blank forms and a proper seal. Welcome to paperwork that doesn't hurt anyone.
Oni is back, under the survivors' agreement.

Nacre's assembly benches, set in a ring around the listening pool. Delegates from Hearthward, Brackenford, Cinderwake, Bellharbor, High Aerie, Veyr and Whitebone. Nobody sits at the head. There isn't one.
We are here to compare what worked. Not what was promised. What worked.
The trial relay at Nacre. Distributed load - the wheel, the cable, the pool. It still runs. Here's the circuit, drawn for anyone to build.
And the consent check. Asked, not assumed; answered, not signed over; revisable, at any time.
Skyspine's mooring anchors hold without anyone on the lever. That's an anchor for the release.
Veyr's registry records who wrote every name. That's an anchor too. Paper, but still.
Whitebone's cells opened on keys their occupants chose. The seals remember. That can be taught.
And every crossing in the Rootward has a named keeper. Nobody carries a whole map alone anymore.
Cinderwake's heat comes from waterwheels and a rota. We've already solved it, you see. Region by region. We don't need a new crown. We need everyone's pieces at once.
Then there is one thing missing: how the activation route actually runs. Who knows it?
Soldiers from three towns bring Rook in. His hands are bound in ordinary rope. He is thinner.
I do.
The hidden route. The fourth relay. Everything I pasted over in the archive diagrams. Here.
I imposed freedom as a command. I told myself it was different from what the ministry did. It was the same shape.
You want forgiveness?
I want to answer for it. After this is done. Not instead.
Then the assembly records it. Extraction was a harm. The forced awakening was a harm. Both require accountability. Neither cancels the other.
The record is written in many hands. Rook signs where he is told to sign, and nowhere else. The soldiers take him to wait for his hearing.
Voss is in the Crown Heart. What is left of him. He has fused himself to the vessel at the centre of the Ember Sea, and he is still trying to make every fragment obey.
Then we go there with everyone's pieces.
The Ash Accord is signed. When you're ready, fly Lanternwake to the Crown Heart in the middle of the Ember Sea.
The Lanternwake crew room has a board of leads - personal matters for each of you, and four strange ones besides. None of them has to be done first.
The pool projects conflicting memories now - dragon and human, overlapping. We set up a listening house. Nobody has to listen alone, or at all.
When your whole crew is together again, come to the assembly benches south of the pool.
You're all here. The assembly is waiting on the benches south of the pool.
Heavier than it was. That's how you know.
The pool showed us the same morning again. I saw a wedding. She saw a funeral. We still argue. We still come every week.
We haven't agreed once. It's the best thing we do together.
Still watering. Still don't know if the plants are sacred. Still don't think it matters.
Salt, jars, remedies. The cloth-lined jars are back in fashion. Everything old is useful again.
The listening house has one rule: you may stop listening at any time. People keep coming back anyway.
The listening house has beds. Quiet after the second bell.
Lanternwake ties up at the Crown Heart - a rib of dragon bone and relay glass rising out of the Ember Sea.
Two lungs. West runs the physical pressure; east runs the name-binding circuit. The locks alternate - west, east, west, east.
Two teams, then. Four and four. Neither team can finish alone and neither can shut the other in.
The swap bells in each lung pass control between the teams whenever you like.
(This is the Accord Dock. You can still leave: Lanternwake is moored behind you. Past the Concord Bridge, the Crown Vessel.)
(A protected backup has been written: "Before the Final Descent". It is kept separate from your slots and from any clear save.)
When ready, use the split lever on the dock to divide into two teams.
Lanternwake's moored and not going anywhere without you. Rest, restock, come back whenever.
Two teams of five. Same stores, same growth, same recovery point here. Anyone left over holds the recovery point.

You've taken the command ledger.

CITIZEN. REPORT FOR REASSIGNMENT. OBEDIENCE WILL BE REWARDED.
It's offering us a reward. How generous.
Its prompts are just words. Ignore them. The screen will name each edict before it lands.
The Regent's Echo sputters. Its voice box repeats 'REWARD' once more, very quietly, and stops.
Wait. Don't wreck it. A machine like that could keep order. Benevolently, this time.
Its authority function comes out. The evidence stays.
The party pulls the authority core and leaves the ledger and the rest of the machine for the archive.

The automaton drones on. Read its command ledger first - you'll want to know what it's been ordering.
In the listening pool there's a voice nobody claims. Not dragon, not human. Excluded from both testimonies.
The listeners taught me a phrase that lets you hear it without taking from it. Here - it's yours. It's in the Crown Heart, they say. A silent alcove off the Concord Bridge.

The alcove off the Concord Bridge. Say the phrase. Then listen.
The pool has one more voice in it now. It doesn't belong to anyone. It sounds happier.
The silent alcove. A figure of folded light, singing without a sound. Its beat shows as pulses of colour on the walls.
Everyone who came here wanted to use me. As a weapon, as a key, as a proof.
I want only to be heard. You will have to earn the quiet to hear it.
(Optional challenge. Watch the beat windows on the walls.)
...You heard. You didn't take. That is all.
(Received Unowned Song.)
